core_obligations: Construct the comparison map asserted in the statement from the universal property of the henselization (proof lines 3266-3280).
Identify the henselization of the product decomposition with the product of the henselizations by comparing the two as limits (proof lines 3281-3305).
Verify that the henselian pair property holds on each side of the comparison, using the Chinese remainder theorem for the ideals involved (proof lines 3306-3325).
Conclude that the comparison map is an isomorphism (proof lines 3325-3330).
proof_roadmap: Build the comparison map from the universal property of the henselization (proof lines 3266-3280).
Use the Chinese remainder theorem to decompose the rings and identify the two candidates for the henselization (proof lines 3281-3305).
Check the henselian pair property on each factor (proof lines 3306-3325).
Conclude that the map is an isomorphism, which is the statement (proof lines 3325-3330).
difficulty_reason: The lemma is a compatibility statement between henselization and decomposing a ring as a finite product, and its proof is a 65-line argument with several moving parts. It builds the comparison map from the statement's universal property, reduces the assertion to verifying that the map is an isomorphism after both rings are identified as limits of diagrams, and uses the Chinese remainder theorem for the ideals involved together with the henselian pair property to show that the completions agree. The argument is written out in full in the source, with the identification of the two sides carried out by explicit diagrams rather than by citation.
